palisade_policy::engine

Module cache 

Source
Expand description

The decision cache (#42).

A bounded, sharded LRU cache of decisions. Repeated launches of the same file by the same principal in the same context skip evaluation.

§Key

CacheKey is (file identity, object type, subject key, context key, policy key):

  • File identity (FileIdentity): the volume serial, file ID, change stamp (change journal USN or last-write time) and size, or the SHA-256 when known. Any write changes the stamp, so a modified file gets a new key even before its change notification arrives.
  • Subject key: a hash of the token SIDs that the policy’s principal rules test, and nothing else (KeyPlan). A policy without principal rules gives every user the same key, so one entry serves them all.
  • Context key: a hash of only the context facts the policy reads: the other user, device and session facts, if any rule tests them, and the device state (mode, connectivity, lockdown). Schedule slots and network location (#38) join it when they exist.
  • Object key: a hash of the object’s facts that do not follow from the file’s identity: its path (one file can have several, through hard links), the path’s alias and ACL, and the path variables. The file’s content facts (hashes, signatures, version resource) follow from its identity and change stamp, and are not hashed again.
  • Policy key: the snapshot’s generation, which changes on every policy swap, so an entry for an older policy can never be found. The bundle’s decision hash (#43) becomes this key once bundles exist.

§Not cached

cacheable leaves out a decision that rests on an unknown fact, one with a prompt (an approval request, a custom notification, a reason prompt or a re-authentication), one made during an override session, one in learning (which must be seen by the learning pipeline every time, #5), and every decision while the clock is not trusted (super::Clock). A probed fact the agent ran out of budget for (condition_timeout, #329) is an unknown fact, so a decision that rests on one is not cached either.

§Invalidation

  • On a policy swap: the generation changes, and the whole cache is purged.
  • On a write, rename or delete notification for a file (super::Engine::invalidate_file): every entry for that file.
  • On logoff (super::Engine::invalidate_session): every entry made in that session.
  • At a deadline (super::Engine::evaluate takes one, such as the next schedule boundary): the entry expires then.
  • After the policy’s decision_cache_ttl_secs (at most 86400).

Expiry uses the monotonic clock, so setting the wall clock back cannot extend an entry.

§Size

Each shard holds at most its share of CacheConfig::max_bytes, counted with ENTRY_OVERHEAD plus the heap size of the decision. The least recently used entries are evicted first. Hits, misses, inserts, evictions and invalidations are counted (CacheStats).

Structs§

CacheConfig
Sizes and lifetimes of the cache.
CacheKey
The key of one cached decision.
CacheStats
What the cache has done, for the hit-ratio metrics.
DecisionCache
The cache. Shared by every thread that evaluates.
KeyPlan
What parts of the context a policy reads, so the cache key covers exactly those (#42).
KeySeed
The secret key of the cache-key hashes: SipHash with a random 128-bit key chosen when the engine starts, so a crafted context cannot be built to collide with another.

Constants§

ENTRY_OVERHEAD
The bytes counted for one entry besides its decision: the slot (key, links, expiry), the map’s entry and its control bytes, and the Arc header, rounded up.

cacheable
Whether a decision may be cached. See the module documentation.
object_key
A hash of the facts of an object that its file identity does not fix: the path, its alias, whether its short name was resolved, whether its volume’s case folding is known, its ACL fact, and the path variables that path criteria expand.
